messages:
emily: Quick proposal — introduce a simple 'handshake lifecycle' for model acceptance + rollforward. Idea: clients send an explicit Accept-Model header, server performs gating checks (SLOs, perf, eval pass) before routing traffic to a new model, and we run phased rollforwards with automated rollback triggers.

devon: quick q — how different is this from pinning? clients today can pin via model param.

emily: good call. Pinning remains valid for customers who want an explicit lock. Handshake is for controlled migrations where we want the platform to gradually adopt a new model while preserving compatibility. Pin = customer-enforced. Handshake = operator-driven rollforward with rollbacks.

jia: sample header example: 
```
curl -H "Accept-Model: redwood/gptx-7b:2026-03-01" \\ 
  -H "X-Client-Id: acme-app" \\ 
  https://api.redwood.inference/v1/generate
```
Also: client can include `Accept-Model: *` to opt into platform-managed rollforwards.

santiago: what are the gating checks we want before flipping traffic to the new model?

emily: proposal: 1) latency SLO stable (p50/p95 within threshold), 2) infra error rate not increased, 3) quality regressions on a pinned eval set within tolerance, 4) memory/kv-cache behavior within expected limits. All must pass for canary to advance.

rohit: rollforward cadence idea: canary windows 1% -> 5% (12h) -> 25% (24h) -> 100% (48h). Rollback triggers: error-rate > 2x baseline, latency p95 +100ms over baseline, or eval-quality drop > 1% on tracked prompts. Auto rollback + page on trigger.

devon: SDK behavior? if client doesn't send Accept-Model, what's default?

jia: default remains current behavior (unversioned default model). We should deprecate implicit defaults over time but give long runway. Short term: SDKs should start supporting an explicit `acceptModel` option and expose rollback hooks.

emily: server-side negotiation pseudo: 
```
if Accept-Model:
  if model_available(Accept-Model): route_to(Accept-Model)
  elif compatible_variant_exists(Accept-Model): route_to(variant) and add header X-RW-Fallback: variant
  else:
    if client_allows_fallback: route_to(default) and add X-RW-Fallback: default
    else: return 409 "model not available, include allow_fallback=true to accept automatic fallback"
```
(This lets us be explicit to clients about fallback behavior and surface when they requested something unavailable.)

ops-bot: [ci] canary pipeline started for model redwood/gptx-7b:2026-03-01 — run id 2026-03-01-canary-001

santiago: fallback semantics question — if we route to a compatible smaller-quantized variant, do we still guarantee response shape and function-calling stability?

emily: must guarantee shape & function-calls. If we can't guarantee compatibility, we should surface it via flags and not roll forward automatically. The compatibility check must be part of model onboarding.

rohit: telemetry reqs: add per-request fields: requested_model, routed_model, rollout_id, canary_bucket. Expose in tracing + bigtable logs for sampling. Need a dashboard to track quality metrics tied to rollout_id.

devon: ops/runbook questions: who is oncall for canary rollforward failures? need a quick rollback button in console + API to pin fallback.

emily: agree. Action items: 
- (emily) write a short design doc with header spec, negotiation rules, fallback semantics.
- (jia) SDK PR to add `acceptModel` option and an opt-in `allowFallback` flag.
- (rohit) wire up telemetry keys and a rollout dashboard prototype.
- (santiago) add model compatibility checklist to onboarding pipeline.
- (devon) add rollback button + API for fast pin.

emily: asking for +1s or objections. If no objections by EOD Friday we'll start a draft doc and prototype the canary pipeline. @devon @jia @santiago @rohit :thumbsup: ?

devon: +1

jia: +1

santiago: +1, quick note: include a compatibility unit test harness in onboarding so every model publish runs the shape & function call checks.

rohit: +1, will sketch telemetry schema tomorrow

emily: thanks all — filing the doc and will ping for reviews.
